note: The frozen half of OER-01. Nothing a submission says may move any number in this file. The verifier reads its own copy of it at grading time.

budget.note: The CEILING on the budget, not the amount every run spends. Every run is allowed at most 3072 micro-batches and no run may exceed it. What this slot grades is how few of them a recipe needs, so a recipe that uses all 3072 has spent the whole ceiling.

init.note: Every run in this task starts from the same parameter tensors. The optimizer recipe is the only thing that differs between two runs.

evaluation.metric: mean token-level cross-entropy in nats, lower is better
evaluation.note: THE GRID IS THE INSTRUMENT OF THIS SLOT. Every run is evaluated after every 128 micro-batches on the SAME 524288-token window, giving 24 measured points across the ceiling. The grid is counted in MICRO-steps -- tokens consumed -- and not in optimizer steps, so two recipes that take different numbers of optimizer steps are still compared at the same points on the token budget. Nothing is interpolated: a crossing is reported at one of the points that was actually measured. The graded split is NOT in the agent image.

target.definition: the shipped environment/default_recipe.json's OWN evaluation loss at the end of the budget ceiling, measured on the grading run
target.note: There is no literal for the target anywhere in this bundle. It is whatever the untuned shipped recipe reaches when it spends the entire ceiling, re-measured from scratch every time the verifier runs. That is what makes the question 'how few tokens do you need to get there' answerable without a stored number.

data.format: FineWeb10B GPT-2 BPE. 1024-byte int32 header (magic 20240520, version 1, token count), then uint16 token ids.
data.train_slice_note: Exactly the 25165824 tokens the ceiling allows, plus one for the shifted target.
